Visual modifications to the lands to the landscape include two trailer courts, three transmission lines, the Burlington Northern rail-road, and County Road 384, and the existing surface coal mine.

Sound
An ambient sound survey was conducted at six locations about Tracts II and III during the period July 26 to August 2, 1975 (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 n). Sound level recordings were made on weekdays and weekends during daytime, evening and nighttime periods as defined by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. The decibel (dB) system describes sounds pressure levels on a logarithmic scale from 0 to 140, 140 dB being the threshold sound level so loud as to be painful. Permanent impairment of hearing can occur at sound levels of 90 dB when exposed for 8 hours or more.
Following are ranges in residual, median and intrusive sound levels measured at a location on Tract II removed from existing mine:
Residual (Level exceeded 90 percent of the time)

Median (Level exceeded 50 percent of the time)

26-29 dB

Intrusive (Level exceeded 10 percent of the time)

30-36 dB

Sound levels at this location were relatively uniform except for sparse, vehicular traffic on local roads.
